why: Rule 1: all three prongs at 19013 start sub-MIP there and rise away (p4 shows the 19032-19013-19031 chain rising monotonically 10k->205k into a proton stopping at 19012, and 19023 rising to 310k at 19014); competing apex 19003 (two long tracks, 21 cm upstream) has the connecting 23.5 cm segment arriving hot, not leaving cool.

Clean V apex at the lowest z of the event: 61 cm pi rises away to a Bragg end at 16005, 116 cm mu leaves the other way, cluster-68 prong points back at it, and the muon far end 16003 carries the Michel-like stubs (rule 3).
Rule 1 unanimous: 3 of 3 prongs rise away (182 cm mu to 116k, 28.6 cm p to 189k, 56 cm p to 208k, all stopping elsewhere), a 1.4 cm fragment sits 5 cm away, and it is at low z (32).
Deg-4 hadronic knot: 12 cm proton rising away to 213k at 16001 plus two very hot short stubs (187k, 160k), with the MIP muon leaving and continuing through 16000 into cluster 49 to stop 185 cm away.

Rule 3 removes 10002: the 7 cm prong there rises monotonically to 217k within 31 deg of the incoming muon (its own Bragg, level matching a muon not a proton) with an 11 cm Michel at the branch, so that is the far end; the zoom shows the 256 cm muon terminating exactly at 10001 where a 163-188k proton pair (cluster 53) originates - muon start plus hadronic prongs.
Deg-3 vertex with a 28.5 cm proton rising away to 175k, a 2 cm 132k stub, and a 139 cm muon leaving downstream; a 2.5 cm fragment sits 5 cm away.

Zoom shows 20004 as the common endpoint of the dark-red 10 cm proton (stopping at 20001, 184k) and of the MIP track that runs up in z through 20008/20010 into the 154+178 cm muon; 20008 3.6 cm away is the only real alternative.

Event is a handful of disconnected dots (rule 8); 19001 is the only multi-prong point, a deg-2 end of the 4.7 cm 226k stopping proton, and the most upstream of that pair, but this is close to a guess.
Rule 1 unanimous 2 of 2: a 97 cm muon rising away to 117k and a 61 cm proton rising away to 220k, both stopping, and the 175 cm EM shower (cluster 126, pi0) starts 12 cm downstream of it.

Rule 1 plus rule 6: 18001 is the only end whose attached segment rises away (67316 -> 93110), and the zoom shows a fan of separate short fragments (clusters 79, 71, 61, 62, 72, 74) converging on it 11-13 cm away; 18002 scores 0 of 2 on rule 1 and carries a genuine monotone 8 cm rise to 225k, i.e. something stops there.

Abstain: the zoom shows the 5 cm 260k segment continuing the 129 cm muon within 16 deg (and at a muon, not proton, level - 125k at 5 cm residual range), so 17002 is a stopping-muon end with a Michel (rule 3), the muon entering at the z=2.7 upstream face; nothing else in the event but two sub-cm dots, so no neutrino vertex is readable.
Deg-3 vertex with two very hot short protons (181k, 196k), a 2.3 cm 175k fragment 1 cm away, and a 198 cm muon rising away to 122k where it stops at 5000.
Only real cluster in the event; p4 shows the 4.7 cm proton rising 110k->240k away from 20002 toward 20001, and 20002 is the deg-3 hub carrying two further stubs.

Zoom shows 7010 as the apex at the lowest z where everything converges: 71 cm mu rising away, 45 cm pi rising away to 150k, the 475 cm muon through 7007, and all the shower clusters (79/72/75/76) opening downstream of it; the 7.4 cm proton reading hot at the vertex is blob contamination.

Rule 8 territory: disconnected low-dQ/dx fragments near the x/y edge with no long track and no real cone (p5 RMS ~1-2 cm); I lean on rule 7 and take the deg-3 hub of the most upstream fragment group (cluster 15, z~232) as the start of the EM activity.
